subject: Culture
title: Lunar New Year Red Envelopes
description: One-minute skill: Lunar New Year Red Envelopes.

hook.text: During Lunar New Year, Chinese elders give children red envelopes stuffed with cash. The color wards off evil.

buildup.text: The tradition traces to a legend where coins tied with red string protected a child from a demon named Sui.

discovery.text: The amount matters: even numbers are lucky, but the number four is avoided because it sounds like 'death.'

twist.text: WeChat's digital red envelope feature sent 46 billion virtual envelopes in 2021. Tradition went cashless.

climax.text: Red envelopes flow upward too—employees give bosses envelopes as thanks, encoding workplace hierarchy.

punchline.text: Even cash gifts carry coded social messages.

quiz.question: Why is the number four avoided in red envelope amounts?
